Head’s Welcome
Welcome to Chafyn Godolphin, an independent school in Salisbury and the city’s only all-through school, where children grow and learn from Nursery through to Sixth Form. With over three hundred years of history, we are a school shaped by our past but firmly focused on the future.
One of our greatest strengths is continuity. We support pupils throughout their entire school journey, building strong relationships and a deep understanding of each individual. This allows us to develop confident, capable young people who are well prepared for life beyond school.
Our approach to learning is centred on “enjoyable challenge”. Pupils are encouraged to aim high, take thoughtful risks, and learn from both success and failure. In doing so, they build not only academic success, but also resilience, curiosity, and kindness.
A strong sense of belonging underpins everything we do. Every pupil is known, valued, and supported from the moment they join us. This foundation gives them the confidence to try new things, contribute fully to school life, and support those around them.
Located on the edge of historic Salisbury in Wiltshire, we offer a unique blend of city culture and countryside access. Our age-appropriate campuses ensure pupils learn in environments suited to each stage of their development, helping them grow in confidence as they progress.
What truly defines Chafyn Godolphin is our people. Our staff inspire, challenge, and support pupils to achieve their best, both academically and personally.
I warmly invite you to visit us, see our school in action, and meet our pupils. There is no better way to experience what makes a Chafyn Godolphin education so distinctive.
Chafyn Godolphin Vision Statement
Every pupil knows themselves, grows in confidence and character, and develops the curiosity, courage and kindness to make a positive difference in the world.

Two Campuses, One School
Why Choose Chafyn Godolphin?
Recently merged, Chafyn Godolphin has become Salisbury’s leading and only co-educational all-through school, Nursery to Sixth Form, offering day and boarding options for prospective families. Ranked in the top 3% nationally for student progress in GCSE’s our value-added score places us in the top bracket nationally making us one of the best performing schools in Wiltshire. Something we are extremely proud of.
We bring together the strengths of two campuses under one united school to offer a seamless educational journey, helping every child grow in confidence, curiosity, kindness with a deep routed sense of belonging. Children at Chafyn Godolphin are academic, artistic, courageous, kind and independent
ENJOYABLE CHALLENGE
The right amount of challenge is a combination of success and failure. It is important that children enjoy both in the right way. Success should lead to confidence, not complacency; failure to reapplication, not disillusionment. Children enjoy correctly pitched challenge, and we prize that as a key ingredient in everything we do.
We are delighted to announce our new partnership with Southampton FC. Read our latest blog post.

Headmaster’s Welcome
Courage, Compassion & Curiosity
WELCOME FROM THE HEAD
An old story has a princess setting her princely suitors a challenge to determine whom she will marry. The princes are blindfolded and asked to identify an object in front of them. They all reach out and hastily announce their answers, which range from spear to snake, with curtain, wall, column and rope all in between. The seventh prince does not reach out at all, but listens to the blundering of his rivals. He works out how their reasoning could possibly fit together and solves the conundrum: “It’s an elephant.”
Whilst this fable offers sage advice about listening, not simply trusting what is before you, it also serves to illustrate the pitfalls of describing a school. Chafyn Grove is made up of many parts, but is not wholly represented by any of them. The enjoyment of challenge, the exercise of compassion, results, facilities and food are each characterful aspects of our identity, but none of them are the entire story. I hope our website gives you as many pieces of our narrative as possible, which can combine to give you the clues you seek as to what distinguishes us as a school from others. To remove the blindfold altogether, I look forward to meeting in person.
My Background
Simon Head spent his Prep School education at Cranmore, in Surrey. Thereafter he went to Stonyhurst then Cambridge, where he read Classics. University was prefaced by a gap year as a platoon commander in the Royal Green Jackets and succeeded by a teaching post at Dulwich College Preparatory School. An ensuing year teaching in up-country Kenya at Pembroke House led to the role of Housemaster, then Deputy Headmaster, at St. John’s Beaumont in Windsor. In 2010 he took over the headship of Moreton Hall in Suffolk, before moving to Chafyn Grove for the September of 2016.
Simon is married to Sarah, who is also a teacher and has two teenage sons. Alongside work Simon enjoys reading novels, walking the dog, football in the garden and fly-fishing.

About Chafyn Godolphin
A New Chapter, Built on Strong Foundations
Under the leadership of new Headteacher Chris Eades, Chafyn Godolphin begins an exciting new chapter.
Built on the strengths of two outstanding schools and united by a shared commitment to educational excellence, Chafyn Godolphin offers families a distinctive and inspiring environment where children can thrive from their earliest years through to adulthood.
We look forward to welcoming you to our community and helping your child realise their full potential.
Our Values
We build a community where every individual is valued and included, where strong relationships create the confidence to grow, take risks and thrive in and beyond the classroom.
We approach challenge with confidence, resilience and a willingness to step beyond our comfort zone, knowing that growth for progress comes from trying, failing and trying again.
Curiosity Encouraged
We encourage every pupil to ask questions, explore ideas and think deeply, developing independence of mind and a lifelong love of learning.
We lead with empathy and respect, creating a community where everyone is known, valued and supported to be themselves.

Facilities Hire
Exceptional Facilities in the Heart of Salisbury
Chafyn Godolphin offer an exceptional range of facilities available to hire throughout the year. Whether you are looking for a venue for sporting activities, performances, conferences, community events, residential courses or holiday programmes, our campuses provide high-quality facilities in beautiful surroundings.
With extensive indoor and outdoor spaces across both the CGS Senior Site and CGS Prep Site, we are proud to support a wide range of local clubs, organisations, schools and community groups.
To discuss availability and hire options, please contact our lettings team or book online through SchoolHire.
Contact us to find out more about hiring our facilities or to discuss your requirements:
lettings@chafyngodolphin.co.uk

Leisure Centre
Located within the beautiful grounds of the CGS Senior Site, our Leisure Centre offers outstanding facilities for both the school community and the wider public.
The Leisure Centre is regularly used by a variety of organisations, including swimming clubs, schools and specialist coaching providers.

Performing Arts Centre
The purpose-built Performing Arts Centre is a professional and versatile venue designed to host performances, concerts, conferences and community events throughout the year.
At the heart of the building is a theatre-style auditorium with seating for up to 290 guests, complemented by a fully equipped stage, professional lighting and sound systems, and a dedicated control room. The venue is air-conditioned for comfort and technician support is available to help ensure events run smoothly from start to finish.
In addition to the main performance space, the centre includes two flexible recital and meeting rooms, a refreshment area and excellent on-site parking, with both main and overflow parking available for visitors.
The Performing Arts Centre is equally suited to large-scale productions and smaller community gatherings. It regularly hosts theatre performances, dance showcases, concerts, conferences, workshops, presentations, school proms and celebratory events.
Used by local performing arts organisations, dance schools and community groups throughout the year, the Performing Arts Centre provides an impressive setting for a wide range of events and occasions.
Main Hall
The Main Hall at the CGS Senior Site is a traditional and characterful venue, distinguished by its oak panelling and striking stained-glass feature window. Combining historic charm with practical functionality, the space offers seating for up to 120 guests and benefits from a Baby Grand Piano, PA sound system, flexible staging options and a balcony overlooking the hall.
The venue is well suited to conferences, talks, lectures, community gatherings, dinners, receptions, music performances and school celebrations. Adjacent classrooms provide additional breakout spaces, making the Main Hall an excellent choice for events requiring multiple meeting or activity areas within a unique and welcoming setting.
Residential Accommodation
The CGS Senior Site offers a range of boarding accommodation options, making it an ideal venue for residential courses, educational visits, training programmes, summer schools and group stays.
Walters House accommodates up to 40 guests and provides a combination of dormitory and twin-room accommodation, with wash facilities available within the rooms.
Cooper House, the largest of the boarding houses, can accommodate up to 97 guests. Offering a mix of ensuite rooms and dormitory-style accommodation, it benefits from generous communal areas and convenient access to dining facilities, making it particularly well suited to larger groups.
Jerred House provides accommodation for up to 64 guests in a combination of twin and single rooms. The house also includes kitchen and conference facilities, flexible social spaces and access to a private garden, creating a comfortable environment for both short and extended stays.
School House provides accommodation for up to 57 guests.
These facilities have successfully hosted language schools, music courses, training organisations and educational groups, offering flexible accommodation in a safe and welcoming setting.

A range of classrooms and meeting spaces are available throughout the year.
These spaces are ideal for training days, meetings, workshops, presentations and educational events.

Sports Hall
The modern two-storey Sports Hall at the CGS Prep Site is a versatile indoor venue suitable for a wide range of sporting activities and community use. Featuring a spectator viewing gallery, changing rooms, shower facilities, accessible amenities and convenient on-site parking, it provides an excellent environment for both training and competition.
Regularly used for badminton, volleyball, indoor hockey, tennis, cricket training, basketball, netball and five-a-side football, the hall is equally well suited to clubs, schools and coaching programmes. A range of sports equipment is included within the hire fee, helping hirers make the most of the facility from the moment they arrive.
Performance Hall
The impressive Performance Hall at the CGS Prep Site is a spacious and flexible venue, ideal for community events, performances, meetings and celebrations. Accommodating up to 250 guests in a theatre-style layout or 300 standing attendees, the hall is equipped with sound and lighting systems, adaptable furniture arrangements and convenient access to nearby parking.
Regularly used for choir rehearsals, presentations, fitness classes, book groups, community events and private parties, it offers a versatile space that can be tailored to suit a wide range of activities.
Pre-Prep Hall
The bright and modern Pre-Prep Hall provides a welcoming and adaptable setting for smaller events and group activities. With direct access to an enclosed outdoor area and convenient nearby parking, the space is particularly well suited to children’s activities, fitness classes, community groups, meetings, workshops and birthday parties.
Its flexible layout and contemporary design make it an ideal venue for organisations seeking a comfortable and practical space for regular sessions or one-off events.
Residential and Whole-Site Hire
During quieter holiday periods, the CGS Prep Site is available for hire in full or in part, making it an excellent venue for residential programmes, educational courses, activity camps and group events. Set within extensive grounds, the site offers a wide range of facilities that can be tailored to meet the needs of schools, organisations and community groups.
Residential accommodation is available for up to 70 guests, complemented by a dining hall seating up to 170 people, a recreation room, commercial kitchen and a selection of classrooms and teaching spaces. Hirers also benefit from access to the site’s excellent sporting facilities, including the Sports Hall, Performance Hall, squash courts, tennis and netball courts, sports pitches and a heated outdoor swimming pool during the summer months.
The adventure playground and outdoor spaces provide additional opportunities for activities and recreation, creating a versatile setting for both educational and residential programmes. Catering and cleaning services may also be available by prior arrangement, helping to ensure a seamless and enjoyable experience for visiting groups.
Outdoor Spaces

We are proud to share our facilities with the wider community and currently welcome a range of sports clubs, performing arts organisations, schools, charities and community groups across both sites.
Whether you are planning a sporting event, residential course, conference, performance or celebration, our experienced team will be delighted to help you find the right space.
To enquire about availability and pricing, please contact our lettings team or visit SchoolHire to make a booking.

Chafyn Godolphin and Southampton FC Unite to Inspire Learning On and Off the Pitch
At Chafyn Godolphin, we are always looking for new ways to enrich our pupils’ education, broaden their horizons and inspire them to achieve their full potential. That is why we are delighted to announce a new affiliate partnership with Southampton Football Club, creating exciting opportunities for pupils to benefit from professional expertise both in and beyond the classroom.
Beginning this academic year, Southampton FC staff will work closely with our pupils and teachers through a weekly programme that combines sport, education and personal development. Alongside specialist football coaching, club representatives will contribute to lessons and co-curricular activities, bringing real-world experiences and industry insight into school life.
More Than Football
While the partnership will undoubtedly enhance our football provision, its impact reaches far beyond the pitch.
Through regular engagement with Southampton FC professionals, pupils will have the opportunity to develop valuable life skills including teamwork, leadership, communication, resilience and problem-solving. These are qualities that support not only sporting success, but academic achievement and personal growth.
By connecting learning with examples from elite sport, pupils will gain a deeper understanding of how important skills can be applied in real-world settings, helping them build confidence and ambition for the future.
Creating Opportunities for Every Child
As a newly co-educational school, Chafyn Godolphin is committed to providing outstanding opportunities for both girls and boys.
This partnership reflects our belief that sport can be a powerful vehicle for learning, personal development and aspiration. By working with one of England’s most respected professional football clubs, we aim to inspire participation, encourage excellence and give pupils access to experiences that broaden their understanding of the opportunities available to them.
Learning from Professional Expertise
The partnership provides access to Southampton FC’s renowned coaching resources, development frameworks and Academy philosophy. Pupils and staff alike will benefit from learning alongside experienced professionals who understand what it takes to develop talent, build character and achieve success.
Just as importantly, pupils will gain insight into the many career opportunities that exist within the sporting world, from coaching and performance analysis to communications, operations, education and leadership.
Looking Ahead
This exciting collaboration represents another step in Chafyn Godolphin’s commitment to providing a broad, forward-thinking education that prepares pupils for a rapidly changing world.
By partnering with organisations beyond the education sector, we continue to create meaningful opportunities that inspire curiosity, raise aspirations and encourage lifelong learning.
We look forward to sharing the impact of this partnership over the coming months as our pupils benefit from unique experiences that connect education, sport and personal development, helping them flourish both at school and beyond.
A Shared Commitment to Development
Commenting on the partnership, Head Chris Eades said:
“We are delighted to be partnering with Southampton Football Club in a collaboration that reflects our commitment to providing outstanding opportunities for all our pupils. As a newly co-educational school, we are especially excited to work with a club that shares our ambition to inspire participation and excellence in sport for both girls and boys.”
“While this partnership will undoubtedly enhance our sporting provision, its greatest strength lies in the wider educational opportunities and future pathways it will create. Having Southampton FC staff working alongside our own colleagues and pupils each week, both in lessons and through our co-curricular programme, will help inspire young people to develop the skills, confidence and ambition needed to thrive in the modern world.”
Tom Grevatt, Head of Football Programmes at Southampton FC, added:
“We’re really pleased to welcome Chafyn Godolphin School to the Southampton FC Affiliate Partnership programme.”
“The partnership will provide the school with greater insight into the way we develop young players at Southampton FC, including access to our famous Academy frameworks, coaching knowledge and elements of our Southampton Way philosophy. We want to share that knowledge and experience to benefit both pupils and staff, helping to inspire young players and support their development both on and off the pitch.”

Academic Life – Prep
A Love of Learning
At Chafyn Godolphin Prep, academic life is designed to inspire curiosity, confidence and develop a lifelong love of learning. From Years 3 to 6, pupils benefit from a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum that encourages them to think independently, embrace challenge and develop the skills they need for future success.
Personalised Support and Expert Teaching
Every child belongs to a form group led by a dedicated form tutor who provides daily guidance, encouragement and pastoral support.
Years 3 & 4: Pupils enjoy the consistency of a form tutor who teaches a significant proportion of the curriculum
Years 5 to 6: Children transition to a specialist teaching model, moving between subject experts who bring enthusiasm and deep knowledge to every lesson.
This carefully structured journey helps pupils develop confidence, independence and strong organisational skills as they progress through the Prep School.
A Broad and Ambitious Curriculum
Learning extends far beyond the core subjects. Pupils explore a rich variety of disciplines, developing creativity, critical thinking and practical skills alongside academic excellence.
Subjects and opportunities include:
Lessons are designed to be engaging, interactive and challenging, ensuring every pupil can achieve their potential.
English and Mathematics
Humanities
Modern Languages
Computing
Art and Design
Drama
Music
Physical Education and Games
Outdoor and experiential learning
Developing Independence
Homework is carefully planned to reinforce classroom learning while helping pupils develop effective study habits and personal responsibility.
An optional supervised Prep session at the end of the school day provides a structured environment where many pupils choose to complete their work before heading home.
Preparing for the Future
Academic life at Chafyn Godolphin Prep is about much more than achieving excellent results. Pupils are encouraged to be inquisitive, resilient and ambitious, developing the confidence to embrace opportunities both in school and beyond.
By combining outstanding teaching, individual support and a wealth of co-curricular experiences, Prep pupils leave ready for the next stage of their educational journey and equipped with the skills to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
FAQs
How are pupils supported academically?
Every pupil belongs to a form group led by a dedicated form tutor who provides guidance, encouragement and pastoral support throughout the school year.
Who teaches pupils in the Prep School?
In Years 3 and 4, pupils benefit from the consistency of a form tutor teaching much of their curriculum. From Year 5 onwards, children are taught by specialist subject teachers.
What subjects do pupils study?
Prep pupils follow a broad curriculum including English, Mathematics, Science, Humanities, Modern Languages, Computing, Art, Drama, Music and Physical Education.
Are there opportunities beyond the classroom?
Yes. Pupils can take part in a wide range of co-curricular activities, with more than 60 options available across sport, creative arts, outdoor learning and special interest clubs.
What enrichment activities are available?
Activities may include bushcraft, sailing, trampolining, cookery, sign language, languages, performing arts and a variety of sporting opportunities.
Is homework set in the Prep School?
Yes. Homework is designed to reinforce classroom learning and help pupils develop good study habits, organisational skills and independence.
Is there a supervised homework session after school?
Yes. An optional supervised Prep session is available after the school day, allowing pupils to complete their homework in a structured environment before going home.
How does the Prep School prepare pupils for the future?
Through a combination of academic challenge, specialist teaching, pastoral support and extensive co-curricular opportunities, pupils develop the confidence, independence and resilience needed for future success.

Chafyn Godolphin Bursaries
Chafyn Godolphin is committed to broadening access to prospective families as well as supporting current families. We offer a limited number of means-tested bursaries. They are awarded on a case-by-case basis and based on financial need, taking into consideration academic ability, and are reviewed annually.
We do not offer full bursaries and parents are expected to make a contribution to the fees. The value of the award is calculated on a sliding scale that takes into account the financial position of both parents’ income and assets. Please note that bursary applications for combined incomes over £75,000 may not be considered.
How to Apply
To apply for a means tested bursary, first you will need to apply for a place at Chafyn Godolphin for your child. We will then work with Bursary Administration Ltd, who administer bursary applications on our behalf, to help guide you through the process.
The deadline for applications for September 2027 entry is Friday 27 November 2026. Bursary decisions are communicated alongside decisions on school places.
Please click here for a copy of our policy on means-tested bursaries.
The Old Godolphin Association also provides one means-tested bursary each year to the child of a former Godolphin pupil. Candidates for the OGA bursary will need to apply via the means-tested bursary process.

Health, Fitness and Wellbeing for the Whole Community
The CGS Leisure Centre is a welcoming hub for health, fitness and wellbeing, serving both the school community and local residents. Located within the beautiful setting of our school campus, the centre provides high-quality facilities in a friendly and supportive environment, helping members of all ages and abilities achieve their personal fitness goals.
Whether you’re looking to improve your fitness, enjoy a relaxing swim, or maintain an active lifestyle, our facilities offer something for everyone. The centre features a modern fitness suite equipped with a range of cardiovascular and strength-training equipment, alongside a 25-metre swimming pool suitable for fitness swimming, training and recreational use.
Our experienced and approachable team is always on hand to provide guidance and support, ensuring that every visit is a positive experience. With convenient on-site parking and flexible membership options, staying active has never been easier.

Welcome to Nursery
We are delighted to welcome children to our Nursery, a bright, inviting space designed to inspire curiosity and creativity. With its own dedicated facility including separate bathroom facilities and direct access to a safe, enclosed playground, our Nursery encourages learning both indoors and outdoors. Children can attend full days, mornings, afternoons, or a flexible combination to suit your family’s needs.
In our happy and nurturing environment, your child will feel safe, valued, and supported as they develop the confidence to explore, experiment, and take risks. Small class sizes and excellent staff-to-child ratios mean that every child receives the attention and guidance they need to grow and thrive.
Our curriculum blends adult-led and child-initiated activities, with plenty of opportunities for free play so children can follow their own interests and shape their learning journey. We offer a broad and balanced programme covering all seven areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage, with specialist teaching in music, drama, French, PE, and swimming. Our wonderful school grounds are extensive and including the woodland area Dingley Dell, the Adventure Playground, and the school garden and allotments all providing endless opportunities for exploration and discovery.
Nursery children also enjoy socialising with Pre-Prep children during the day, sharing playtimes, and joining them for a freshly made, nutritious hot lunch in our dining room.
Coming in January 2027 – Chafynch Nursery
We are delighted to announce that our current nursery provision is getting a new home and rebrand. Launching in January 2027, the new provision will see our nursery open to children up to the age of 4 years, across multiple rooms with capacity for over for over 50 children.

Funded Early Education (FEE)
In partnership with Wiltshire County Council, Chafyn Godolphin offers the Funded Early Education (FEE) grant. This is available up to a maximum of 15 hours per week, for six terms, from the term after a child’s third birthday and is subject to the completion of the relevant SCC Declaration Form each term.Our funded hours are provided in the mornings between 8.30am and 11.30am. If you are not claiming FEE hours from an alternative provider the 15 hours will be fully funded and there will be no extra cost. Parents/carers may use the Tax Free Childcare to access funding.
Fee information can be found here.

FAQs
What will happen on my child’s first day at Nursery?
You will be greeted by our Nursery teacher as you arrive who will run through the drop off routine with you (signing in, unpacking bags etc). We find most children settle quickly, but appreciate this can be difficult for both parties sometimes. Please communicate any concerns you have in advance so that we can make arrangements to accommodate them.
What will my child be given to eat during the day?
We are very aware of the need to promote ‘healthy eating’. Nutritious lunches are provided by our school’s catering team, ensuring a healthy balance of sweet and savoury, as well as encouraging children to try new tastes and textures. Morning and afternoon snacks are provided each day, with milk on offer to drink in the mornings if children would like it. Water is readily available at all times throughout the day for anyone who is thirsty.
My child has a special diet. Can this be catered for?
Yes – Chafyn Godolphin caters for a wide range of allergies and specific diets.
Can my child still have a nap after lunch?
Yes – we have a number of options available to children to enable this.
What will happen if my child becomes ill during the day?
Our on-site medical matrons are available to assist with any child who is taken ill during the day. Parents will be contacted should they need to go home. Children are asked to remain at home for 48 hours following any sickness or diarrhoea.
What qualifications do staff have?
Our Nursery staff are qualified at level 3 or above. In addition, all Early Years staff hold full Paediatric First Aid qualifications and Food Safety & Hygiene qualifications, as well as being up-to-date with safeguarding training.
How do you communicate with parents?
We see most parents/carers at the beginnings and ends of days and these regular, informal meetings enable us to chat to you about how your child is getting on and to deal with any questions quickly and easily. Our fortnightly Pre-Prep newsletter gives details of some of the activities the children have been up to, as well as providing information about upcoming events, and parents can also follow us on Facebook and Instagram. We have two scheduled Parents’ Meetings during the academic year, providing an opportunity for us to get together to review your child’s learning and progress. All staff are contactable by email and additional meeting can be arranged if you would like them.
What government funding is available?
In partnership with Wiltshire County Council, Chafyn Godolphin offers the Funded Early Education (FEE) grant. This is available up to a maximum of 15 hours per week, for six terms, from the term after a child’s third birthday. Our funded hours are provided in the mornings between 8.30am and 11.30am. Parents/carers may also use the Tax Free Childcare to access funding.
Can I adjust the sessions I have arranged?
Of course. We are happy to make changes and additions wherever possible (subject to availability).
Do I have to wait for an Open Day to visit?
No – every day is an Open Day. If you would like to visit outside of our termly ‘’Open Days’ or ‘Stay & Play’ days, please contact the school office to arrange a date and time.
Contact Admissions Today: Start Your Journey
How much will it cost to attend?
Full details of our fees can be found here.
Do you provide any discounts?
Yes. We have a military discount available and we also provide a sibling discount. Please get in touch to discuss.

Beyond the Classroom – Prep
Discovering Passions, Building Confidence
Life at Chafyn Godolphin Prep extends far beyond the classroom. We believe that a truly exceptional education is about discovering passions, developing confidence and encouraging every child to embrace new experiences.
Whether performing on stage, creating artwork, learning a musical instrument, representing the school in sport or taking on a new challenge, pupils are encouraged to explore their interests and develop the skills that will stay with them long after they leave Chafyn Godolphin.
Performing Arts
Drama is a vibrant and much-loved part of school life. From the earliest Nativity performances through to major productions for older pupils, children are encouraged to develop confidence, creativity and communication skills through performance.
Every pupil receives a weekly drama lesson, learning techniques such as improvisation, devising and effective vocal performance. As they progress through the school, opportunities to perform continue to grow, with productions, showcases and musical performances providing pupils with regular opportunities to take to the stage and express themselves.
For those wishing to pursue their passion further, individual LAMDA lessons are available. These sessions can focus on acting, musical theatre, Shakespeare, speaking verse and prose or presentation skills, helping pupils develop confidence in public speaking, performance and self-expression while working towards recognised qualifications.
Music
Music is woven throughout life at Chafyn Godolphin Prep and provides opportunities for every child to discover the joy of performance and music-making.
From choirs and orchestras to jazz ensembles and string groups, pupils are encouraged to participate, perform and collaborate from an early age. Informal concerts throughout the year provide regular opportunities to showcase musical progress in a supportive environment, helping children build confidence and develop a love of performing.
Pupils can also benefit from individual instrumental tuition with specialist teachers across a wide range of instruments, including piano, voice, strings, woodwind, brass, percussion and guitar. Whether learning for enjoyment or working towards examinations and qualifications, every child is supported on their own musical journey.
Music begins early, with all Year 2 pupils learning violin and recorder as part of their class curriculum, providing a valuable introduction to instrumental learning and music reading.
Art, Craft & Design
Creativity flourishes at Chafyn Godolphin Prep. Through Art, Craft and Design, pupils are encouraged to experiment, explore and express themselves while developing both technical skills and creative confidence.
Each week, pupils enjoy dedicated art lessons that introduce a wide range of disciplines, from painting and drawing to sculpture, ceramics, textiles, printmaking and design. As pupils move through the school, they gain access to increasingly specialist techniques and facilities, allowing them to broaden their artistic skills and discover their individual strengths.
Our dedicated Art Department includes specialist studio spaces, a pottery studio and a woodwork room, providing inspiring environments where creativity can thrive. Alongside practical skills, pupils learn to analyse, discuss and appreciate works of art, developing visual literacy and a deeper understanding of the creative world around them.
Sport
Sport plays an integral role in daily life at Chafyn Godolphin Prep and is central to our commitment to developing confidence, leadership, resilience and teamwork.
Pupils enjoy a broad sporting programme supported by outstanding facilities, including a sports hall, swimming pools, AstroTurf pitches, tennis and netball courts, cricket grounds, squash courts, rugby and football pitches, fitness suite, and a climbing wall. Through training, fixtures, tournaments and tours, children are encouraged to challenge themselves while enjoying the many benefits of being active.
Our pupils regularly compete against other schools and participate in regional and national competitions, with a strong tradition of sporting success across a variety of disciplines. We are equally proud of those taking their first steps in sport as we are of those competing at the highest levels, with all pupils encouraged to participate, develop their skills and enjoy representing the school.
Outdoor Learning & Wellbeing
Outdoor learning is an important part of life at Chafyn Godolphin Prep, encouraging pupils to explore, discover and develop a love of the natural world. From our dedicated Forest School area, Dingley Dell, to gardening projects and hands-on outdoor activities, children benefit from regular opportunities to learn beyond the classroom. Through initiatives such as Nature Ninjas and our annual Wellbeing Week, pupils also develop resilience, confidence and an understanding of the importance of physical and emotional wellbeing, all while having fun and embracing new experiences.
A Programme for Everyone
Every child at Chafyn Godolphin Prep is encouraged to make the most of the opportunities available to them. Whether performing in a production, learning a new instrument, creating artwork, competing in sport or tackling a new challenge, pupils are supported to explore their interests, discover hidden talents and develop the confidence to try something new.
These experiences enrich school life, create lasting memories and help pupils grow into capable, well-rounded young people who are ready to embrace whatever comes next.
FAQs
What performing arts opportunities are available at Chafyn Godolphin?
Pupils enjoy weekly drama lessons, school productions, showcases and musical performances throughout their time at the school. Opportunities begin from an early age and increase as pupils progress through the school.
Can pupils take LAMDA lessons?
Yes. Individual LAMDA lessons are available and can focus on acting, musical theatre, Shakespeare, speaking verse and prose, or presentation skills. Pupils can also work towards recognised qualifications.
What music opportunities are available?
Music is a key part of school life, with opportunities to participate in choirs, orchestras, jazz ensembles, string groups and regular concerts throughout the year.
Can pupils learn a musical instrument?
Yes. Individual instrumental lessons are available with specialist teachers across a wide range of instruments, including piano, voice, strings, woodwind, brass, percussion and guitar.
Do younger pupils receive instrumental tuition?
All Year 2 pupils learn violin and recorder as part of their class curriculum, helping them develop early instrumental and music-reading skills.
What art facilities are available?
The Art Department includes specialist studio spaces, a pottery studio and a woodwork room, giving pupils access to a broad range of creative experiences and materials.
What sporting facilities does the school offer?
Pupils benefit from extensive facilities including a sports hall, swimming pools, AstroTurf pitches, tennis and netball courts, cricket grounds, squash courts, rugby and football pitches, a fitness suite and a climbing wall.
Do pupils compete in sports fixtures and competitions?
Yes. Pupils regularly represent the school in fixtures, tournaments and competitions, including opportunities at regional and national level.

Welcome to Prep School
Our Pre-Prep
The Pre-Prep department sits within the Prep School, with its own dedicated corridor and outdoor area for learning and play. We welcome children aged 3 to 7 years. Our small class sizes with a high ratio of teachers to pupils is something of great value. This enabling environment provides the best learning experience for our children, promoting curiosity, creativity and a caring approach in all we do.
A distinctive quality of our Pre-prep is that while they have their own dedicated area, they also have full access to the rest of the school. For instance, from Year 1 the children visit the Art block, enabling a far greater range of experience. Whilst the form tutor remains the primary teacher, specialists are used for Forest School, Music, Games, French and ICT.
A range of school trips are enjoyed which complement the school curriculum with a generous helping of fun. These can be local trips, to the cathedral for example, or further afield on the school minibuses to Brownsea island. Every experience is designed to stimulate a love of learning and the school’s core values of Belonging, Courage, Curiosity and Kindness.
Prep School
At Chafyn Godolphin Prep School, children are encouraged to be curious, embrace new experiences and grow into confident, happy learners who are excited about the world around them.
Through inspiring teaching, enjoyable challenge, outstanding pastoral care and a wide range of opportunities both inside and outside the classroom, every child is supported to discover their strengths, develop their talents and build self-confidence. We nurture a love of learning, independence and resilience, helping children to flourish academically, socially and emotionally.
As they progress through the Prep School, children are challenged and supported in equal measure, developing the skills, character and confidence needed for a successful transition to senior school and beyond.

FAQs
DO I HAVE TO WAIT FOR AN OPEN DAY TO VISIT THE SCHOOL?
No, every day is an ‘Open Day.’ Whilst we operate specific open days each term, we recommend that a visit on any other day probably offers even better insights.
Contact Admissions Today: Start Your Journey
WHAT IF I CAN’T TAKE MY CHILD TO SCHOOL? DO YOU HAVE BUSES?
Yes – details available from the school office and here
CAN MY CHILD COME EARLY OR LEAVE LATE FROM SCHOOL?
Our basic wraparound care runs from 8am till 6pm; it is possible to extend this range as needed (without having to become a boarder)
DO YOU HAVE ENTRY TESTS INTO THE SCHOOL?
No. A discussion with the admissions team before joining helps us ensure that all your child’s needs can be fully met from day one.
DO I HAVE TO WAIT UNTIL SEPTEMBER FOR MY CHILD TO START AT CHAFYN GODOLPHIN?
Not at all. Such a decision is always determined by what is best for the child – we prefer children to start with us as soon as possible.
WHAT WILL HAPPEN ON MY CHILD’S FIRST DAY AT SCHOOL?
A peer buddy helps them navigate; you will have been talked through the process well in advance.
IS THERE A PARENTAL NETWORK?
There is a formal system of year group representatives, as well as a series of informal ones too.
WHAT LANGUAGES DO YOU TEACH?
French, Spanish and Latin. others (eg. Russian or Ancient Greek) regularly appear as clubs for different parts of the year.

Pre-Prep
Why choose our Pre-Prep in Salisbury
In the Pre-Prep department we ensure that every child has the opportunity for enjoyable challenge. The chance to explore opportunities both inside and outside of the classroom and a chance to fulfil their potential. We place the same value on our outdoor learning environment to allow children to have equality of opportunity in their learning both inside and outside. Across the school site we have a range of places to learn and play including an adventure playground, dingily dell, large playing field, pond and woodland play equipment.
Pre-Prep benefit from year-round swimming lessons either at the Prep site during the warmer months in our outdoor heated pool and for the rest of the year, the children swim at the indoor pool at the senior site.
From the Early Years (Nursery and Reception), to Key Stage 1 (Year 1 and Year 2) the children play, eat and learn together. The interaction between the year groups is just one of the qualities of an all-round education at Chafyn Godolphin. Each Monday, the whole school – from Reception to Year 6 – celebrates the week’s accomplishments together in assembly.
Homework is introduced in Year 1 and includes spellings to learn and a practical task each week, and daily supported reading is encouraged. There is a weekly swimming lesson for each class in Pre-Prep in our own pool for half of the year, and year round for Years 1 and 2.

Academic Life – Prep
A Love of Learning
At Chafyn Godolphin Prep, academic life is designed to inspire curiosity, confidence and develop a lifelong love of learning. From Years 3 to 6, pupils benefit from a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum that encourages them to think independently, embrace challenge and develop the skills they need for future success.
Personalised Support and Expert Teaching
Every child belongs to a form group led by a dedicated form tutor who provides daily guidance, encouragement and pastoral support.
Years 3 & 4: Pupils enjoy the consistency of a form tutor who teaches a significant proportion of the curriculum
Years 5 to 6: Children transition to a specialist teaching model, moving between subject experts who bring enthusiasm and deep knowledge to every lesson.
This carefully structured journey helps pupils develop confidence, independence and strong organisational skills as they progress through the Prep School.
A Broad and Ambitious Curriculum
Learning extends far beyond the core subjects. Pupils explore a rich variety of disciplines, developing creativity, critical thinking and practical skills alongside academic excellence.
Subjects and opportunities include:
Lessons are designed to be engaging, interactive and challenging, ensuring every pupil can achieve their potential.
English and Mathematics
Humanities
Modern Languages
Computing
Art and Design
Drama
Music
Physical Education and Games
Outdoor and experiential learning
Developing Independence
Homework is carefully planned to reinforce classroom learning while helping pupils develop effective study habits and personal responsibility.
An optional supervised Prep session at the end of the school day provides a structured environment where many pupils choose to complete their work before heading home.
Preparing for the Future
Academic life at Chafyn Godolphin Prep is about much more than achieving excellent results. Pupils are encouraged to be inquisitive, resilient and ambitious, developing the confidence to embrace opportunities both in school and beyond.
By combining outstanding teaching, individual support and a wealth of co-curricular experiences, Prep pupils leave ready for the next stage of their educational journey and equipped with the skills to thrive in a rapidly changing world.
FAQs
How are pupils supported academically?
Every pupil belongs to a form group led by a dedicated form tutor who provides guidance, encouragement and pastoral support throughout the school year.
Who teaches pupils in the Prep School?
In Years 3 and 4, pupils benefit from the consistency of a form tutor teaching much of their curriculum. From Year 5 onwards, children are taught by specialist subject teachers.
What subjects do pupils study?
Prep pupils follow a broad curriculum including English, Mathematics, Science, Humanities, Modern Languages, Computing, Art, Drama, Music and Physical Education.
Are there opportunities beyond the classroom?
Yes. Pupils can take part in a wide range of co-curricular activities, with more than 60 options available across sport, creative arts, outdoor learning and special interest clubs.
What enrichment activities are available?
Activities may include bushcraft, sailing, trampolining, cookery, sign language, languages, performing arts and a variety of sporting opportunities.
Is homework set in the Prep School?
Yes. Homework is designed to reinforce classroom learning and help pupils develop good study habits, organisational skills and independence.
Is there a supervised homework session after school?
Yes. An optional supervised Prep session is available after the school day, allowing pupils to complete their homework in a structured environment before going home.
How does the Prep School prepare pupils for the future?
Through a combination of academic challenge, specialist teaching, pastoral support and extensive co-curricular opportunities, pupils develop the confidence, independence and resilience needed for future success.

Chafyn Godolphin Scholarships
Our scholarship programme recognises talent, potential and commitment, while providing opportunities that help students develop their strengths and pursue their passions.
Scholarships Available
Year 7, Year 9 and Year 12 (Sixth Form) Entry
Senior School scholarships are awarded for the duration of a student’s time in the Senior School. Sixth Form scholarships remain in place throughout a student’s Sixth Form studies.
Students awarded Art & Design, Drama or Music scholarships are expected to continue studying their specialist subject through to GCSE (for Year 7 and Year 9 scholars) or A Level (for Year 12 scholars).

Academic Scholarships
Assessment
Year 7 & Year 9 Applications: Candidates will be required to attend the Scholarship Assessment Day and Academic scholarship interview in January. They will be required to show a high level of technical accuracy in their writing as well as a confident ability to write creatively and understand written text and perform well in our cognitive ability tests and at interview.
Year 12 (Sixth Form) Applications: Candidates will be interviewed by a member of the Senior Leadership Team as part of the application process.

Our Academic scholars have a natural curiosity and a passion for understanding the world. They are encouraged to question, analyse and explore – from the nature of humanity to the science of our planet and the vastness of the cosmos – growing into thoughtful, informed young people with study skills that will support their university and future careers.
Our Inspiring Bright Minds programme encourages scholars to think deeply, explore widely and enjoy the excitement of learning. It helps students discover new interests, challenge themselves and develop the confidence to pursue their passions.
Art & Design Scholarships
Assessment
Candidates should be able to demonstrate a genuine interest in art and design, both within and beyond the classroom. They must show exceptional skill in recording from first-hand observation, using a wide range of materials, techniques, and processes. In addition, candidates should provide clear evidence of sustained engagement and a deep passion for the subject.
Year 9 Application: All candidates are set an Art & Design project on the Year 9 application deadline date. This comprises of an A4 sketchbook which contains a set of instructions and a design brief which the applicant should undertake and complete in the weeks running up to the interview date. This sketchbook, plus a portfolio of their own work, is brought to interview and forms the basis of the discussion with the Art Department.
In the portfolio, we would like to see the greatest range of work possible this could include two-dimensional painting and drawing, textile design, printmaking, graphics, photography and three-dimensional studies, ceramics, and sculpture. If you have studied design technology, you may like to bring examples of this work along also. We will be looking for candidates who have a wide variety of materials, techniques and processes evident in their portfolio of work. We only want to see work completed within the last two years.
Year 12 (Sixth Form) Application: Candidates must be predicted a 7, 8 or 9 grade at GCSE. All candidates are expected to bring a portfolio of their GCSE Art & Design work to an interview.

Available at Year 9 and Year 12 (Sixth Form) entry
Being an Art Scholar offers students the opportunity to push their creative boundaries beyond the scope of everyday academic life. Our Art scholars are at the heart of a dynamic, award-winning department renowned for its innovation and excellence within the artistic community. We celebrate not only artistic ability but also a distinctive way of seeing and interpreting the world through art, craft and design. Our Art scholars set the creative pulse of the department – inspiring others to reach new heights in their own artistic journeys.
Drama Scholarships
Assessment
Drama scholarships are open to any student with a passion and flair for the Performing Arts. To be considered for a Drama scholarship, students must send in a video of a learned contemporary monologue from a published play – no longer than two minutes long. The deadline for this to be submitted is Friday 15 January 2027.

Participate in a Drama workshop

Becoming a Drama scholar is more than just an award – it’s an invitation to join a vibrant, creative community where your child’s talents will be nurtured and celebrated. As a Drama scholar, your child will gain access to a wealth of opportunities designed to develop their confidence, creativity, and leadership skills – attributes that will benefit them for life, both on and off the stage.
Exceptional training and qualifications:
Exclusive experiences
Performance Opportunities
A Drama scholarship is about more than just performance – it’s about building confidence, communication, and resilience. We are committed to nurturing your child’s love of drama, helping them to grow as artists and individuals, and inspiring a lifelong passion for the performing arts.
Music Scholarships

Music scholarships recognise and nurture musical promise. Above all, we seek applicants who demonstrate enthusiasm, passion, and a genuine commitment to music. While technical ability is important, it is potential and dedication that truly stand out.
As a guide, candidates should be performing at approximately the following levels:

Chafyn Godolphin has a long-standing musical tradition, and our Music scholars are at the heart of that. Their dedication and skill have won prizes in national competitions and the opportunity to perform in some of the most prestigious locations. Music Scholarships at CGS provide a comprehensive package of opportunities, designed to support each scholar’s musical and personal development.
Sports Scholarships
Assessment
Sports scholarships are awarded to pupils who demonstrate exceptional ability in one or more sports. As a guide and depending on the sport, candidates should be performing at approximately to the following levels (evidence to support this will be required):
Candidates are invited to submit further written evidence and a sporting CV. Shortlisted candidates will then be invited to attend an assessment day where fitness levels will be tested and skills, techniques, knowledge and understanding will be assessed. This will be in sports-specific sessions and will include an interview with a member of the PE department.

Sport at Chafyn Godolphin is about more than competition – it’s about personal growth, teamwork and pride in shared achievement. Our athletes regularly compete at regional and national levels, showcasing dedication, teamwork and excellence across a range of sports.
Year 7 and Year 9 scholars must be fully committed to at least two winter sports teams and one summer team, and Year 12 (Sixth Form) scholars must be fully committed to at least one sport, and to squad training and fixtures during the week and at weekends.
Our Sports scholars lead by example, demonstrating outstanding commitment, preparation and attitude both in training and competition. They also play a key role in mentoring younger teams, sharing their experience and guidance. Our Sports scholarship package includes the following for successful candidates:
At Chafyn Godolphin, there are two levels of Sport Scholarship available: Podium and Podium Potential.
Candidates offered a Podium Sport scholarship benefit from more individually-focussed sessions for Strength and Conditioning and will have access to an extended lecture series on a range of topics including Sport Psychology, Lifestyle Coaching and Injury Prevention Training. Podium Potential Scholars will receive group Strength and Conditioning sessions and will be invited to attend our lecture series.
Chafyn Godolphin reserves the right to amend the level of scholarship awarded to each candidate at any time throughout the school year.
